note: The main banks, chosen as the best-known large card issuers (no central bank ranking was read): National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr and CIB. National Bank of Egypt's card pages answered behind a Cloudflare check and CIB's behind an Incapsula check on 2026-10-30, and neither was read. Banque Misr's credit card fees, usage limits, commissions and interest rates (dated 1 September 2026), read in full on 2026-10-30 (first read 2026-10-29 for the Classic alone): each personal credit card's issuance fee for the first year and its renewal fee, equal for every card but El Araby's and written as a yearly fee (Classic, Islamic Classic, Gold and Islamic Gold 250 pounds, Titanium 350, Platinum 500, Signature and World 2,500, World Elite and Visa Infinite 8,000, Visa Infinite Private free; El Araby 100 to issue and 50 to renew, written as a yearly fee of 50 waived for the first year and an issue fee of 100). The conventional cards bear 4% a month on a decreasing balance; the Islamic cards and El Araby 20.55% a year, fixed. A cash withdrawal at Banque Misr's ATMs costs 2% with a minimum of 15 pounds on the conventional cards and 5% with a minimum of 50 on the Islamic ones (other banks' and foreign ATMs cost more and aren't written); the 'outside fees' on cash and purchases abroad are 3%; the late payment and overdrawn fees are 75 pounds each. The Business card isn't written (not a personal card), nor the Islamic Titanium, whose fee column the table doesn't print separately, nor the Asatha card, whose interest rate the table doesn't give, nor the instalment card. The schedule states no minimum payment or grace period; interest on purchases runs from the purchase date only on the unpaid amount.
